The higher-authority business evidence supports prioritizing the **regulated mid-market and enterprise segments**, not education startups. The quantitative segment analysis in [NL-016#NL-016-S03] explicitly states that mid-market (28 accounts) and enterprise (9 accounts) generate 83.8% of recurring revenue, with low churn (enterprise 1.3%, mid-market 2.1%) and high NPS (enterprise 52, mid-market 47). It directly notes that "while our sales playbook (NL-009) previously highlighted education startups as a high-growth sector, our metrics prove that smaller startups (such as EduVantage Labs) show weak long-term retention compared to regulated mid-market and enterprise companies" [NL-016#NL-016-S03]. The same conclusion is confirmed in executive discussion: CEO Maya Patel states "our Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) is regulated mid-market and enterprise organizations" and that SMB churn (4.8%) is "too high to support sustainable growth" [NL-015#NL-015-S03].

The trade-off is **longer, more complex onboarding and higher acquisition costs**. Enterprise onboarding takes a median of 8.7 weeks and mid-market 5.2 weeks "due to permission and security complexities" [NL-016#NL-016-S03]. Enterprise CAC averages $22,000 (vs. $3,000 for SMB), though it yields a superior LTV:CAC of 16.0x versus SMB's 8.3x [NL-016#NL-016-S03]. The sales discussion also notes enterprise deals involve "massive security reviews or permission-mapping audits" and longer sales cycles, requiring teams to "navigate their security reviews" [NL-015#NL-015-S03].
